passages.quote: In December of 2023, the first set of federal bail reforms — Bill C-48, the bail and sentencing reform act — received royal assent and came into effect in January of 2024. Bill C-48 of 2023 was supposed to fix catch-and-release justice in B.C. The act was going to make bail stricter and harder to get, including cases of repeat and violent offending. It would also create new circumstances of reverse onus.

passages.title: Hansard 2026-03-03 pm: Attorney General Ministry estimates debate (Sturko)
passages.quote: Proposed amendments would require consecutive sentences for violent auto thefts, break and enter, extortion and arson and allow them for violent repeat offending as well, meaning that one person could serve their sentence one after another, instead of serving their sentences for multiple offences at the same time. In March of 2024, the B.C. prosecution service released a report with further data on bail. They reviewed 4,800 bail hearings between November 2022 and December of 2023.

passages.title: Hansard 2026-02-24 pm: Budget debate (Sturko)
passages.quote: This includes $73 million to support the courts, sheriffs, Crown counsel, legal aid and the judiciary; $16 million for a new chronic property-offending intervention initiative, targeting vandalism and shoplifting hurting small businesses; $26 million to continue the repeat violent offending initiative, which is already reducing police interactions and speeding up charge approvals; $24 million for specialized investigative and enforcement programs to help address street disorder and connect individuals to needed services. passages.title: Hansard 2026-02-24 pm: Budget debate (Sturko)
passages.quote: The riding of Ladysmith-Oceanside is made up of a number of small towns in rural areas, where people choose to live the small-town life so that they can leave their doors unlocked and their car keys on the passenger seat and know their neighbour. passages.title: News Release: CentreBC sets five hard conditions for any Northern Pipeline

passages.title: BC Conservatives Elect Hard Right Leader
passages.quote: Our Values Our Policy Resources Get Involved Become a Member Make a Donation Volunteer News Contact BC Conservatives Elect Hard Right Leader May 30, 2026 CentreBC Warns of Deeper Polarization FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE May 30, 2026 VANCOUVER — CentreBC leader Karin Kirkpatrick today responded to the election of Kerry-Lynne Findlay as leader of the BC Conservative Party, warning that her victory signals a further shift away from the political centre at a time when British Columbia desperately needs practical, unifying leadership. “The leadership race was ultimately a choice about the future direction of the Conservative movement in British Columbia,” said Kirkpatrick.
